274 work items titled 'Test item for show' / 'Test item for show JSON' (descriptions 'Testing wl show' / 'Testing wl show command') were found in the idea stage, all with default priority (medium), no tags, no assignee, and issue type empty. All 274 were soft-deleted on 2026-08-06 (see deletion reason below) but the source that created them is still unknown and will keep polluting the worklog on every run.

## Problem statement

Something — almost certainly a test script, demo, or CLI verification routine — repeatedly creates real worklog items as a side effect of exercising `wl show`. The items were created between 2026-08-04T00:09:35Z and 2026-08-06T12:30:59Z, spanning multiple days and short ID-prefix sequences (WL-0MSDWI97..., WL-0MSDWSV25..., WL-0MSDWSVE...) suggesting rapid, scripted creation. No source was found in the ContextHub repo (searched for 'Test item for show' in ts/js/sh/py/md — no hits).

## Goal

Find the source (likely in the worklog project repo, or an agent skill/test harness) that creates these items, and ensure it cleans up after itself so the worklog is not polluted.

## Suggested investigation leads

- Search worklog repo (and ~/.pi/agent/skills, ~/.pi/agent/commands) for 'Test item for show', 'Testing wl show', 'wl create' invocations in test files and scripts.
- Look for tests exercising `wl show` that create a real item without deleting it afterward.
- Check test teardown/cleanup logic: tests should create items in an ephemeral .worklog dir or delete created items in teardown.
- Item creation window (Aug 4-6 2026) may correlate with recent commits in the worklog repo — check git log for that window.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The source that creates the 'Test item for show' work items is identified and documented in a comment on this item.
- AC2: The source no longer creates persistent items (either it cleans up after itself, or it is removed/fixed).
- AC3: No new items matching 'Test item for show' / 'Test item for show JSON' appear in the worklog for 7 days after the fix lands (or: the fix commit is linked in a comment on this item).

## Problem

Duplicate work items are created by e2e tests running against the real worklog DB:
- `tests/e2e/headless-tui.test.ts`: 'Test item for show' (265) + 'Test item for show JSON' (266) — 531 items created 08-01..08-07, no cleanup teardown. Still present in 3 stale worktrees.

Sync-clobber bug reverts soft-deletes (known in WL-0MSPZP7FE009YXPG), and `wl doctor prune` has never been run (778 soft-deleted items accumulate).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1**: `tests/e2e/headless-tui.test.ts` has teardown that deletes created items (or the test is removed if no longer needed)

## Problem

`wl doctor prune --days N` hard-deletes items locally, but the next `wl sync` re-adds them all from the remote ref, because `mergeWorkItems` (src/sync.ts) re-imports every remote item missing locally (`if (!localItem) { mergedMap.set(remoteItem.id, remoteItem); }`). There is no `--no-pull` and prune has no push/rewrite path.

## Observed (2026-08-13)

- Ran `wl doctor prune --days 0` → 1,034 items hard-deleted locally (2941 → 1907 items)
- Ran `wl sync` → 'Work items added: 1034' — all resurrected from `refs/worklog/data` (back to 2941)
- Net result: prune is a no-op in a synced setup; items remain soft-deleted forever (the 'deleted but not pruned' backlog)

## Proposed fix

Add `--push` (or auto-push) to `wl doctor prune` that, after hard-deleting locally, rewrites the remote worklog ref with the pruned local state — mirroring `doctor foreign-items --apply --push` which already uses `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (src/sync.ts:1130).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl doctor prune --days N --push` leaves the remote ref without the pruned items
- [ ] A subsequent `wl sync` does NOT resurrect the pruned items
- [ ] `--dry-run` unchanged; default remains no-push (safe)
- [ ] Unit/integration test covers prune+push against a temp git repo
data.title: wl doctor prune cannot persist: sync re-adds pruned items from remote ref

# Prune and rotate stale audit_debug JSONL files across worklog stores

**Issue type:** chore (maintenance/tooling) · **Priority:** critical · **Parent:** none

## Problem statement

Legacy `audit_debug_*.jsonl` forensic dumps have accumulated in worklog stores
on this host — ContextHub `.worklog` holds **48 files / 12.5 GB** (store total
13 GB) and `open_source_llm/.worklog` holds **33 files / 11.3 GB** (store total
11 GB), with single files up to ~1.9 GB last written 2026-08-01. A further
**2.5 GB** sits under `~/.audit_debug/`. These files make recursive greps read
multi-GB inputs (observed ~4.4 GB read, 12+ minutes, ~48% CPU) and inflate every
worklog/audit operation. No automation prunes either location, so the growth is
silent and unbounded.

## Users

- **Agents/operators running greps and audits on this host** — "As an agent
  running quality gates, I want stale debug dumps pruned and size-bounded
  automatically so scans stay fast and predictable."
- **Maintainer/producer** — "As a maintainer, I want retention enforced by
  automation (not one-off manual cleanups) so disk usage cannot silently reach
  tens of GB again."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Retention sweep is implemented and unit-tested.** A repo-local script at
   `scripts/prune_audit_debug_logs.py` discovers `audit_debug_*.jsonl` files
   under every `~/projects/*/.worklog/` store and under `~/.audit_debug/**`, and
   selects for removal those older than `--older-than` days (default **7**) **or**
   larger than `--max-size` MB (default **50**). It is dry-run by default;
   `--apply` performs deletion. Pytest tests cover: age boundary, size boundary,
   non-matching filenames are never touched, missing root is a no-op, dry-run
   changes nothing, and `--apply` deletes exactly the selected set.
   *Verification:* `pytest tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py` passes.
2. **Legacy backlog is reclaimed.** Running the sweep with `--apply` removes all
   legacy `audit_debug_*.jsonl` files from ContextHub `.worklog` (48 → 0) and
   `open_source_llm/.worklog` (33 → 0), reclaiming **≥ 20 GB**. Before/after
   aggregate counts and `du -sh` figures are recorded as a work-item comment.
   *Verification:* `ls <store>/audit_debug_*.jsonl` returns nothing for both
   stores; total reclaimed size recorded.
3. **Recurrence is prevented by automation.** A daily cron entry (installed by
   an idempotent `scripts/install-audit-log-hygiene.sh` helper, or documented as
   a copy-paste `crontab -l` snippet when auto-install is declined) runs the
   sweep with `--apply` and appends to a bounded log under `~/.audit_debug/`.
   Re-running the sweep immediately afterwards reports **no candidates**
   (idempotent). A `--check` mode exits non-zero when the post-sweep total
   debug-log footprint exceeds a configurable budget, suitable for manual or
   hook-driven use. *Verification:* unit tests assert exit codes for `--check`
   under/over budget; a second `--apply` run reports zero candidates.
4. **Policy and runbook are documented.** A docs page
   (`docs/dev/audit-debug-log-retention.md`) states the retention policy
   (locations, thresholds, dry-run/apply semantics, cron install and removal,
   safety guarantees, and the `~/.audit_debug` vs legacy `.worklog` distinction)
   and is linked from the relevant docs index. *Verification:* file exists and
   is linked; documented commands are copy-paste runnable.
5. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes** (code
   comments, README/docs site entries) **and the full project test suite passes
   with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Destructive-by-explicit-flag only.** Default is dry-run; deletion requires
  `--apply`. Only files matching `audit_debug_*.jsonl` are ever considered.
- **Never touch tracked or live data.** `.worklog/*` is git-ignored, but the
  sweep must not touch `worklog.db`/WAL/SHM, `config.yaml`, worktrees, or any
  non-debug file. Live SQLite worklog data is unaffected.
- **Repo boundaries.** Do **not** edit the SorraAgents-owned audit skill
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/audit`, `skill/audit`) or other agent-infrastructure
  directories as part of this item. The existing
  `audit/scripts/cleanup_debug_logs.py` (14-day retention over `~/.audit_debug`,
  dry-run default) is **referenced, not forked**. Upstreaming the `~/.audit_debug`
  half into that skill is a follow-up, not scope.
- Deletions must be resilient to `OSError` (skip and continue, never abort the
  whole sweep) and must emit an audit line per removed file.
- Only aggregate counts/sizes are recorded in work-item comments — never log
  contents (forensic data may include provider payloads).
- **Scope-creep guard:** the broader machine-hygiene skill
  (WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ) and any pre-commit/pre-push enforcement beyond a
  documented optional `--check` call are out of scope; record as follow-ups.

## Existing state

- `audit_runner.py` (SorraAgents `skill/audit`) now writes debug logs to
  `~/.audit_debug/<project-slug>/` (`_debug_log_dir`/`_default_debug_log_path`)
  and deletes them on a successful run (`_remove_debug_log`). New logs therefore
  no longer land in `.worklog/`, so the 24 GB in the two worklog stores is stale
  legacy data that will not regrow.
- `cleanup_debug_logs.py` already sweeps `~/.audit_debug` (files >14 days,
  dry-run default, `--apply` to delete) but is **not automated** and does **not**
  cover legacy `.worklog` locations.
- No cron entry exists for audit-log pruning (only an `llm-wiki` job is present).
- `.gitignore` ignores `.worklog/*`, so legacy files are untracked and safe to
  delete; repo scan helpers (`audit/scripts/scan.py`) already exclude
  `**/audit_debug_*.jsonl` and `.audit_debug/**`.

## Desired change

1. Add a self-contained retention script (Python, stdlib-only) with the
   discovery, age/size selection, dry-run/apply, and `--check` semantics above.
2. Add pytest coverage for selection, safety, idempotence, and exit codes.
3. Add an idempotent cron-install helper plus documentation; optionally surface
   a `--check` call from an existing hook as a non-fatal warning.
4. Reclaim the existing backlog with a recorded before/after.
5. Document the policy/runbook.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/prune_audit_debug_logs.py` — **new**: discovery + age/size selection +
  dry-run/`--apply`/`--check`; mirrors `cleanup_debug_logs.py` conventions.
- `scripts/install-audit-log-hygiene.sh` — **new**: idempotent cron entry
  installer (with `--remove`), logging to `~/.audit_debug/hygiene-cron.log`.
- `tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py` — **new**: pytest unit tests over a
  temp directory tree (age boundary, size boundary, dry-run, apply, check mode).
- `docs/dev/audit-debug-log-retention.md` — **new**: policy + runbook.
- `.gitignore` — **review**: confirm `.worklog/*` already covers these paths
  (expected: no change needed).
- `.githooks/pre-push` — **optional**: non-fatal `--check` warning (only if the
  producer opts in; otherwise out of scope).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — placement:** tooling lives in ContextHub `scripts/` (this
  item's home repo) and is machine-scoped via `~/projects/*` discovery, rather
  than editing the SorraAgents-owned audit skill. *Open to producer redirection.*
- **Assumption — delete over archive:** the seed permits "archive … or delete";
  we delete, because these are transient forensics already documented as such by
  the audit skill and the reclaimed volume (≥20 GB) is the point. If cold
  storage is required, add a `--archive-dir` (gzip) variant before deletion.
- **Risk — over-broad glob.** A loose pattern could match non-debug files; the
  `audit_debug_*.jsonl` prefix/suffix guard and tests mitigate this.
- **Risk — deleting useful forensics.** Retention is age/size based; files
  newer than the threshold are kept. The 7-day/50 MB defaults are aggressive but
  match the seed; they are CLI-configurable.
- **Risk — scope creep** into machine hygiene / hooks. Guarded above; extras
  become linked follow-up items.
- **Assumption — default retention:** 7 days / 50 MB per the seed, with a
  total-footprint `--check` budget (proposed: 5 GB) documented and configurable.

## Related work

- **WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ** — Create a machine-hygiene skill that evaluates
  performance pressure and proposes remediations (explicitly references this
  item as a root cause; the manual analysis that discovered the runaway grep).
- **WL-0MKTLALHV0U51LWN** — Reduce sync output; add rotating logs (completed;
  precedent for rotating-log handling in `wl sync`).
- SorraAgents `skill/audit/scripts/cleanup_debug_logs.py` — existing retention
  sweep for `~/.audit_debug` (referenced, not forked).
- SorraAgents `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — already excludes
  `audit_debug_*.jsonl` / `.audit_debug/**` from scans.
- SorraAgents `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_debug_log_dir` (moved
  logs out of `.worklog/`), `_remove_debug_log` (deletes on success).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No blocking interview was required** — the seed context (work item
  description) specified the strategy, thresholds (7 days / 50 MB), locations,
  and automation mechanism (cron) sufficiently to draft this brief.
- Q: Where should the retention tooling live, given the audit skill is owned by
  the SorraAgents repo? — Answer (agent, documented assumption): this item's home
  repo, ContextHub `scripts/`, with machine-scoped discovery; marked as an
  assumption open to producer redirection. Source: repo inspection
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/audit` → `SorraAgents/skill/audit`; ContextHub `skill/`
  has no audit skill) + work-item seed.
- Q: Archive to cold storage or delete? — Answer (seed context): either is
  acceptable; **delete** selected as the default with an `--archive-dir` escape
  hatch if cold storage is later required. Source: work item description
  ("archive older files to cold storage or delete").
- Q: What automation mechanism? — Answer (seed context): **cron-based** daily
  `--apply` sweep, plus a `--check` mode for manual/hook use. Source: work item
  description ("implement a cron-based rotation").
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** – Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items without a valid audit (completed)
- **WL-0MSAWAQNM006PAVJ** – Plugin delegates to shared resolver (completed)
- **WL-0MKRSO1KD1NWWYBP** – Persist Worklog DB across executions; refresh from JSONL when newer (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: abort, acceptable, acceptance, add, again (+307 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: abort, add, again, age, agent (+258 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: abort, add, again, age, agent (+254 more)

# Pane-Triage Skill: Approval-Gated Idle Pane Cleanup

## Problem Statement

Agents that end with `</end_session>` leave their herdr pane open, causing idle panes to accumulate and hold memory/CPU. The automatic reaper (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3) handles unattended closure, but producers need a manual, workspace-scoped, approval-gated companion to review and close idle panes — particularly for panes with pending producer review or other special cases.

## Users

**Producer** — Runs several herdr workspaces with active agents. Wants to:
- *As a producer, I want `/skill:pane-triage` to scan my current workspace and report idle vs active panes, with work-item context and producer-review status, so I can decide which panes to close.*
- *As a producer, I want the skill to show a log tail for each idle pane, so I can verify completion before approving closure.*
- *As a producer, I want to explicitly approve or select which panes to close, so I retain full control.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/skill:pane-triage` resolves the invoking workspace from `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (fallback `herdr pane current`) and reports only that workspace.
2. Idle classification uses the **shared classifier** (`classifySession` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts`) — the last non-empty session entry must be an assistant message ending with `</end_session>` (`.trimEnd()` then `endsWith('</end_session>')`).
3. The report renders Idle and Active tables (tab, title, pane id) and, for idle items, the work item id (parsed from pane label) and `needsProducerReview` value.
4. Each idle item's last 20 log lines are printed under the heading `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
5. A "Recommended to close" table lists idle panes and excludes the invoking pane (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) and panes with `needsProducerReview=true`; the never-close guard applies universally (manual and automatic).
6. No pane is closed without explicit producer approval (`yes`/`select`); `no`/ambiguity closes nothing; the invoking pane is never closed.
7. Approved panes are **re-verified** idle immediately before closing via re-read of `herdr pane list`; any pane that became active is skipped with a reason in the Closed ledger.
8. Offline fixture tests cover classification (via shared classifier), marker-mid-message rejection, work-item id parsing, `needsProducerReview` mapping, recommendation rules, and approval gating (no approval → zero close calls).

## Constraints

- **Shared classifier is mandatory** — do NOT reimplement idle state logic. Import `classifySession` and `extractFinalAssistantText` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts`.
- **Shared reaper deps for closure** — import `createHerdrReaperDeps` and `runReaper` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` for pane enumeration and closure.
- **Never-close guards** (from classifier, universal): `implement` panes, items with `needsProducerReview=true`, the invoking pane, and panes with live child processes are never closed — **by both the automatic reaper and the manual skill** (producer confirmed).
- **Approval gate is mandatory** — this is the manual complement to the automatic reaper; it never closes anything unattended.
- **Workspace-scoped only** — no cross-workspace roll-up.
- **Skill placement**: Global skill at `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` (symlinked via `~/.pi/agent/skills/`). Tracked in ContextHub.

## Existing State

- **Shared classifier** (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3): `classifySession()`, `extractFinalAssistantText()`, `DEFAULT_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000`, `SessionSample` type, `CloseDecision` type.
- **Reaper orchestration** (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3): `runReaper(deps, options)`, `ReaperDeps` interface with `listPanes()`, `closePane(paneId)`, `terminateProcessGroup(pid)`.
- **Production wiring** (WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3): `createHerdrReaperDeps(io)`, `parseHerdrPaneCloseList()`, `paneKindFromLabel()`, `paneItemIdFromLabel()`, `readFinalAssistantEntries()`.
- **Dependency**: `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM → WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3` (completed, in_review).

## Desired Change

A new global skill `/skill:pane-triage` that:
1. Enumerates tabs and panes in the current workspace
2. Classifies each pane using the shared classifier
3. Enriches idle panes with work-item context and producer-review status
4. Displays a structured markdown report
5. Prompts for approval before closing
6. Re-verifies panes immediately before closing
7. Logs closure results in a per-pane ledger

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/SKILL.md` — Skill specification (what the agent reads)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/scripts/pane-triage.py` — Main skill script (invoked by agent)
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/scripts/pane_triage.py` — Python module with core logic:
  - `resolve_workspace()` — get workspace ID from env or `herdr pane current`
  - `enumerate_panes(workspace_id)` — call `herdr tab list` + `herdr pane list`
  - `classify_panes(panes)` — use shared classifier via `createHerdrReaperDeps`
  - `build_report(idle_panes, active_panes, invoking_pane_id)` — markdown output
  - `prompt_approval(recommended_panes)` — blocking prompt: yes/select/no
  - `close_panes(pane_ids)` — re-verify and close, one at a time
  - `parse_workspace_id()` — extract from `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`
  - `get_needs_producer_review(item_id)` — call `wl show --json` to check
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/pane-triage/tests/test_pane_triage.py` — Offline fixture tests

## Related Work

- **WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3** — Implement closure reaper script (shared classifier, reaper orchestration, production wiring) — **COMPLETED**, dependency satisfied.
- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — Log all dispatches and auto-close all completed dispatch panes (dispatch monitor) — completed.
- **WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN** — Implement auto-close logic with implement exception — completed.
- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion — evaluated for deferral to this skill.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Should this skill live in the global skills directory or ContextHub-local? — A: **Global** at `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` (tracked in ContextHub), so it is available to all agents. ContextHub-local would limit availability.
- Q: How should a Python skill consume the TypeScript shared classifier? — A: **Producer (Q-OPEN-1):** Add a `--json` output mode to `runReaperCli` in ContextHub; the Python skill shells out to the compiled CLI. Keeps skill Python-only. Source: producer reply (intake).
- Q: May the manual skill close `needsProducerReview=true` panes after approval? — A: **Producer (Q-OPEN-2):** Never close — the never-close guard applies universally (manual skill + automatic reaper). Source: producer reply (intake).
- Q: How should the work-item id be parsed from the pane label? — A: Use the shared `paneItemIdFromLabel()` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` — matches trailing ` - <PREFIX>-<HASH>` pattern.
- Q: Should `needsProducerReview` use the shared reaper deps or a direct `wl show` call? — A: Direct `wl show <id> --json` call in the skill script (the shared reaper deps' `getNeedsProducerReview` is for the reaper's injected I/O; the skill can call wl directly).
- Q: What is the exact idle classification check? — A: Use the shared `classifySession()` from `pane-close.ts` — it implements the `.trimEnd()` then `endsWith('</end_session>')` check. The skill must NOT re-implement this logic.
- Q: How should the skill handle herdr CLI errors? — A: Fail-closed: clear error message, no partial mutation. If `herdr pane list` fails, report the error and exit.
- Q: What happens if a pane becomes active during the approval prompt? — A: The re-verify-before-close step (AC7) handles this: re-read `herdr pane list` immediately before closing and drop any pane that is no longer idle.

## Open Questions (needs producer input)

### Q-OPEN-1 — How should a Python skill consume the TypeScript shared classifier?

**Context.** Skills in `SorraAgents/skill/` are Python-only (`~/.pi/agent/skills`
symlinks to `SorraAgents/skill`; no skill currently ships TypeScript/JS). The
mandated shared classifier, `classifySession` / `extractFinalAssistantText`, and
the reaper (`createHerdrReaperDeps` / `runReaper`) live in TypeScript at
`packages/herdr/src/pane-close*.ts` and compile to `packages/herdr/dist/`. There
is no standalone `herdr` CLI triage command and no `bin` entry, so there is no
current cross-language invocation path.

**Why it matters.** The spec says "import `classifySession` ... do not copy its
logic into the skill", but a Python module cannot import TypeScript. The choice
determines file layout, build/test story, and part of the effort estimate.

**Options.**

1. **Thin Node bridge (preferred).** Ship `scripts/pane-triage-bridge.mjs`
   which imports the compiled `dist/pane-close-herdr.js` + `pane-close.js`,
   enumerates panes, and emits a JSON report (classification + session tail) to
   stdout. The Python skill owns rendering, the approval prompt, re-verification
   and the ledger. Reuses the classifier verbatim; adds one non-Python script to
   a skill (unprecedented but small).
2. **Add a `--json` output mode to `runReaperCli`** in ContextHub and have the
   Python skill shell out to the compiled CLI. Keeps skill Python-only, but
   enlarges the shared surface (and the reaper is currently only wired into the
   herdr plugin, not exposed as a standalone binary).
3. **Write the skill in TypeScript/Node** under `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/`.
   Direct imports, but breaks the Python-skill convention and repo tooling.

**Preferred (needs confirmation):** Option 1.

### Q-OPEN-2 — May the manual skill close `needsProducerReview=true` panes after approval?
